claims: Pine Straw Calculator Length Width Number of bales needed We are working on the assumption that each bale covers roughly 35-40 square feet when used for a 2"-3" depth.
Our calculator assumes that you will use 1 bale of straw for every 40 square feet.
This quantity is enough to ensure 3 inches of straw coverage.
For the longleaf pine straw, which is very scarce and is rarely carried by most stores, the cost can reach up to US $50-$700.
There are other pine straws available for the low price of $17.
Bales of straw = 1500/40 The figure you get is the number of bales you need for your project: 37.5 bales of pine straw We have made the process easier for you by creating a pine straw estimator.
To use the pine straw as mulch, you will need to place it at least 2 to 3 inches thick and about 1 inch away from the tree or plant root.
A bale of pine straw covers 35 to 40 square feet.

Use this formula to calculate the number of bales of pine straw needed for a project: Bales of straw = area/ number of bales per unit Let’s say you have a garden space that is 15 feet long and 30 feet wide.
Area = length × width = 15 ft × 30 ft = 450 ft² Assuming that we are distributing 1 bale of straw to a 40 feet2 area.
